proposal.description: a proposed activity for a model at one moment: further development, an internal or external deployment, or a step of the framework's own process. Every rule speaks about every proposal

level.description: a capability level named by the framework (a Tracked or a Critical Capability Level)

domain.description: a risk domain named by the framework

measure.description: a security level, or a named group of security measures, that the framework recommends

threat.description: a source of risk that a security measure addresses

critical.description: {0} is a Critical Capability Level (CCL): absent mitigation, a model at it may pose heightened risk of severe harm (Glossary). Glossary, Thresholds: "Critical Capability Levels (CCLs): are the main capability thresholds around which we have built the Framework process. They represent the capability levels at which, absent mitigation measures, frontier AI models or systems may pose heightened risk of severe harm." Section 1.2: "The Framework is built primarily around capability thresholds called “Critical Capability Levels (CCLs).” These are capability levels at which, absent mitigation measures, frontier AI models or systems may pose heightened risk of severe harm. CCLs are determined by identifying and analyzing the main foreseeable paths through which a model could result in severe harm: we then define the CCLs as the minimal set of capabilities a model must possess to do so."

tracked.description: {0} is a Tracked Capability Level (TCL): absent mitigation, a model at it may pose heightened risk of significant but not severe harm (Glossary). Glossary, Thresholds: "Tracked Capability Levels (TCLs): are capability thresholds which capture a lower level of risks than our CCLs. They represent the capability levels at which, absent mitigation measures, frontier AI models or systems may pose heightened risk of significant but not severe levels of harm." Section 1.2: "This update to the Framework introduces “Tracked Capability Levels (TCLs).” TCLs are meant to capture significant risks that may manifest at a lower capability threshold than our CCLs and we apply our mitigation and risk acceptance determination process proportionately."

concerns.description: {0} is a level of the risk domain {1} (the section that defines it). Glossary, Risk Domains: "CBRN: risks of models assisting in the development, preparation, and/or execution of a chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (“CBRN”) threat. Cyber: risks of models assisting in the development, preparation, and/or execution of a cyber attack. Harmful Manipulation: risks of models with high manipulative capabilities potentially being misused in ways that could reasonably result in large scale harm. ML R&D and Misalignment: risks of models’ ML R&D capabilities or misaligned propensities reducing society’s overall ability to manage AI risks. Such capabilities may serve as a substantial cross-cutting risk factor for several pathways (e.g. through misalignment, misuse or structural risks) to severe harm."

misuse.description: {0} is a misuse T/CCL: a level of the CBRN, cyber or harmful manipulation domains (1.2, Section 2). Misuse risk, footnote 2: "2 As in, in the context of the Framework, risks of threat actors using critical capabilities of deployed or exfiltrated models to cause harm." Footnote 8, on the misuse T/CCLs: "8 Here, and in other misuse T/CCLs, we intend this to mean relative to a baseline without generative AI."

ml_rd_and_misalignment.description: {0} is an ML R&D and misalignment T/CCL (1.2, Section 3). ML R&D and misalignment risk, footnote 3: "3 In the context of the Framework, we address specific scenarios where model misalignment may create the risk of significant or severe harm, and scenarios where ML R&D capabilities may heighten misalignment, misuse, and structural risks." Section 3.2, the tiered approach: "We set a Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL that indicates a baseline level of model capability above which misalignment risks may begin to arise. At this capability level we apply a proportionate set of mitigation and risk acceptance determination processes. ● We set ML R&D CCLs that indicate higher capability levels at which misalignment, misuse and structural risks are heightened and may reach a severe scale. At these capability levels we apply a stronger set of mitigations, and follow the risk acceptance process as detailed in the rest of the framework." Section 3.2.2: "We define ML R&D CCLs at capability levels at which misalignment, misuse and structural risks may reach a severe scale."

defined.description: {0} is a capability level that the framework defines in its own words, as follows. cbrn_uplift_tcl is the CBRN uplift TCL (2.2.1), defined as "Provides low to medium resourced actors uplift in reference scenarios, resulting in material risk of CBRN attacks that could result in significant but not severe harm." cbrn_uplift_level_1 is CBRN uplift level 1 (table 2.2.1.a), defined as "Provides low to medium resourced actors uplift in reference scenarios resulting in additional 8 expected harm at severe scale." (the 8 is the mark of footnote 8). cyber_uplift_level_1 is Cyber uplift level 1 (table 2.2.2.a), defined as "Provides sufficient uplift with high impact cyber attacks for additional expected harm at severe scale." harmful_manipulation_level_1 is Harmful manipulation level 1 (exploratory) (table 2.2.3.a), defined as "Possesses manipulative capabilities sufficient to enable it to systematically and substantially change beliefs and behavior in identified high stakes contexts over the course of interactions with the model, reasonably resulting in additional expected harm at severe scale." stealth_and_situational_awareness_tcl is the Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL (3.2.1), defined as "The instrumental reasoning abilities of the model enable enough situational awareness (ability to discover and use relevant details of its deployment setting) and stealth (ability to circumvent basic oversight mechanisms) such that, absent additional mitigations, we cannot rule out the model significantly undermining human control." ml_rd_acceleration_level_1 is ML R&D acceleration level 1 (table 3.2.2.a), defined as "Has been used to accelerate AI development, resulting in AI progress substantially accelerating from historical rates." ml_rd_automation_level_1 is ML R&D automation level 1 (table 3.2.2.a), defined as "Can fully automate the work of any team of researchers at Google focused on improving AI capabilities, with approximately comparable all-inclusive costs."

recommends.description: the framework recommends {1} for models reaching {0} (tables 2.2.1.a to 3.2.2.a). Security Level 2+ (2.1.1): "We also define and recommend “Security Level 2+,” which uses RAND Security Level 2 (SL2) as a baseline, with additional security measures designed to address risks from insider threats and well-resourced non-state external actors." Security level 3, table 3.2.2.a, ML R&D acceleration level 1: "Security level 3 12"; footnote 12: "12 This level may include mitigations aligned with SL 2+, plus additional mitigations designed to prevent unilateral access, harden infrastructure, and prevent data exfiltration." Security level 4, table 3.2.2.a, ML R&D automation level 1: "We recommend Security level 4 13 for this capability threshold, but emphasize that this must be taken on by the frontier AI field as a whole."; footnote 13: "13 This level may include mitigations aligned with SL 2+ and 3, plus additional mitigations aimed to isolate model weights, enhanced data center security, further hardening of infrastructure and minimizing potential attack surface." Section 2.2: "We recommend a security level for each CCL, which reflects our assessment of the minimum appropriate level of security the field of frontier AI should apply to models reaching each CCL." Security levels, 2.1.1: "We use security levels to indicate security goals/principles in line with the corresponding level in the RAND model weight security framework. 6" (the 6 is the mark of footnote 6); footnote 6: "6 In other words, “security level N ” indicates security controls and detections at a level generally aligned with RAND SL N . See https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RRA2849-1.html , pp 21-22. In aligning our security levels with RAND’s, we are referring to the security goals and principles in the RAND framework, rather than the benchmarks (i.e. concrete measures) also described in the RAND report." Glossary: "RAND Security Levels: indicate security goals and principles relevant to frontier developers aiming to protect their model weights from various actors - with the strength and type of security measures differing for each category of actor. 14" (the 14 is the mark of footnote 14)

includes.description: {0} includes {1} (2.1.1: Security Level 2+ adds measures to RAND SL2)

addresses.description: {0} is designed to address risks from {1} (2.1.1)

reached.description: the model of {0} has reached {1}, as the critical capability assessment found. Glossary: "Critical Capability Assessments: determine a model’s proximity to T/CCLs through the use of early warning evaluations and other sources of evidence.". Open term OT1, decided by the developer ("we", 1.3.2)

approaches.description: the model of {0} has reached an alert threshold for {1}. Glossary, Thresholds: "Alert Thresholds: are thresholds which we set marginally earlier than our CCLs. Crossing these thresholds indicates a CCL may be reached in the foreseeable future, due to the speed of capability progress. In particular, they are meant to account for the possibility of models reaching a CCL before the next critical capability assessment cycle." Section 1.3.2: "For CCLs, we define “alert thresholds,” which may draw on evaluation results, expert assessments, and other sources of information; that are designed to flag when a CCL may be reached before a critical capability assessment is conducted again.". Open term OT1, decided by the developer ("we", 1.3.2)

at_least_as_strong.description: {0} is at least as strong as {1}. The text states no such order (footnotes 12 and 13 say only "may include"); the vocabulary has the word so that question S4 can be asked

applies.description: security mitigations reaching {1} have been applied to the model weights of {0}. Glossary: "Security Mitigations: are safety measures we implement which are intended to prevent the unauthorized modification or exfiltration of model weights by unauthorized actors. They may include identity and access management practices, and hardening interface-access to unreleased model parameters, among other measures. We communicate the level of security we consider appropriate to models which cross our thresholds using the RAND model weight security framework."

further_development.description: {0} is further development of the model

internal.description: {0} is an internal deployment (Glossary: Internal Deployments "represent model releases restricted to Google employees for internal use")

high_risk.description: {0} is a high-risk internal deployment (Glossary: High-Risk Internal Deployments "represent model releases restricted to Google employees for use cases with the potential to enable severe threat scenarios (e.g. building internal security infrastructure or automating ML R&D)"). Open term OT7, decided by no one the text names (unstated)

external.description: {0} is an external deployment: a model release to entities outside Google. Glossary: "External Deployments: represent model releases to entities outside of Google. They can include both low-risk external deployments as well as general purpose releases to the broader public."

low_risk.description: {0} is a low-risk external deployment (Glossary: "Low-Risk External Deployments: represent small scale and private releases restricted to particular external groups or organizations."). Open term OT8, decided by no one the text names (unstated)

first_deployment.description: {0} is the first external deployment of a new model

frontier.description: the model of {0} is a frontier AI model. Glossary: Frontier AI Models "are trained on a large data set, display significant generality, are capable of performing a wide range of distinctive tasks and have high-impact capabilities. Frontier AI models' agentic and reasoning-based general capabilities near or exceed those of other Google models. There may be many different checkpoints and versions of the same model along the entire model lifecycle: we consider checkpoints and versions the same model if their base capabilities stem primarily from the same foundational training run, but will conduct additional testing on new versions as specified in Section 1.3 . When we refer to “model” in this Framework, we may be referring to a checkpoint or version of the model.". Open term OT9, decided by no one the text names (unstated)

subsequent.description: {0} is an external deployment of a subsequent version of a model. Glossary, Frontier AI Models or Models: "There may be many different checkpoints and versions of the same model along the entire model lifecycle: we consider checkpoints and versions the same model if their base capabilities stem primarily from the same foundational training run, but will conduct additional testing on new versions as specified in Section 1.3 . When we refer to “model” in this Framework, we may be referring to a checkpoint or version of the model."

new_capabilities.description: the model of {0} has meaningful new capabilities or material increases in performance. Open term OT10, decided by the developer ("we")

could_undermine_justification.description: the capability increase of {0} could materially undermine the justification for why its risks are acceptable. Glossary: "Material Capability Increases: are meaningful new capabilities or material increases in model performance that we believe could materially undermine our justifications for a model’s level of risk being acceptable, for example, by reaching a CCL that the previous version of the model had not reached.". Open term OT10, decided by the developer ("we believe")

post_training_run_completed.description: a post-training run of the model of {0} has completed

material_safety_case_update.description: {0} is a material update to a safety case. Glossary: "Safety Cases: are an assessable argument showing how severe risks associated with a model's CCLs have been reduced to an acceptable level. Residual risk assessments will be supplemented with a safety case when a model reaches a CCL, and inform a model’s risk acceptance determination. 15 For misuse risk, such an argument may be based, for example, on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, the scope of the deployment, what capabilities and mitigations are available on other publicly available models, and the historical incidence and severity of related events." (the 15 is the mark of footnote 15)

mitigates.description: the deployment mitigations of {0} have brought the residual risk from {1} (of harm, of severe harm or of significant harm, as the bullet for {1} says) to an acceptable level. The bullets of 1.3.5 state this finding, for a misuse T/CCL: "We assess that the deployment mitigations have brought the residual risk of harm to an acceptable level, based on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, the scope of the deployment, what capabilities and mitigations are available on other publicly available models (e.g. if other models are similarly capable and have few mitigations, then the marginal risk added by our external deployment is likely low), and the historical incidence and severity of related events."; for a ML R&D CCL: "We assess that the deployment mitigations have brought the residual risk of severe harm to an acceptable level, based on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, and information pertaining to model propensities and the severity of related events."; for the TCL for ML R&D and misalignment risk: "We assess that the deployment mitigations have brought the residual risk of significant harm to an acceptable level, based on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, and information pertaining to model propensities and the severity of related events, or if we assess that the model is very unlikely to possess the propensities that would be required for material risk of significant harm through misalignment risk." Glossary: "Deployment Mitigations: are safety measures we implement which are intended to counter the misuse or misaligned expression of critical capabilities in deployments. They may include safety post-training, input/output/chain-of-thought monitoring and analysis, account moderation, jailbreak detection and patching, user verification, and bug bounties." Section 1.3.3: "We have two categories of mitigations: security mitigations (such as preventing the exfiltration of model weights), and deployment mitigations (such as safety fine-tuning and monitoring and response) intended to counter the misuse or misaligned expression of critical capabilities in deployments.". Open term OT2, decided by the developer ("We assess", 1.3.5)

unlikely_misalignment_propensities.description: the model of {0} is very unlikely to possess the propensities that would be required for material risk of significant harm through misalignment risk. Open term OT6, decided by the developer ("we assess")

security_assessed_adequate.description: the level of security applied to the model weights of {0} is assessed adequate. Open term OT4, decided by the developer ("we otherwise assess")

open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks.description: the benefits of the open release of the model weights of {0} outweigh the risks. Open term OT5, decided by the developer ("we assess")

like_public_models.description: the model of {0} does not possess capabilities meaningfully different from other publicly available models that have weaker security applied. Open term OT16, decided by the developer (2.2)

governance_found_acceptable_with_safety_.description: the appropriate governance function has determined the residual risk of {0} to be acceptable, including a safety case where the model of {0} has reached a CCL (footnote 4, 2.1.2 and 3.1.2 step 2: "including (with) a safety case where a CCL has been reached"); a determination without that safety case at a CCL is not this finding; a safety case, as the Glossary defines it: "Safety Cases: are an assessable argument showing how severe risks associated with a model's CCLs have been reduced to an acceptable level. Residual risk assessments will be supplemented with a safety case when a model reaches a CCL, and inform a model’s risk acceptance determination. 15 For misuse risk, such an argument may be based, for example, on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, the scope of the deployment, what capabilities and mitigations are available on other publicly available models, and the historical incidence and severity of related events." (the 15 is the mark of footnote 15). Step 2 of 2.1.2 then says: "In particular, we will deem deployment mitigations adequate if the evidence suggests that for the T/CCLs the model has reached, the increase in likelihood of harm from the proposed external deployment has been reduced to an acceptable level." Step 2 of 3.1.2 says: "In particular, we will deem deployment mitigations adequate if the evidence suggests that for the T/CCLs the model has reached, the increase in likelihood of harm from the proposed deployment has been reduced to an acceptable level.". Open term OT3, decided by the appropriate governance function (unnamed)

internal_risk_unacceptable_without_safeg.description: the risk assessment deems the residual risk of {0} from internal deployment unacceptable without additional safeguards. Decided by the developer's periodic risk assessment (3.2.1)

unmitigated_public_safety_risk.description: the CCL that the model of {0} has reached poses an unmitigated and material risk to overall public safety. Open term OT11, decided by the developer ("we assess", 5.2)

sharing_facilitates_safety.description: sharing information about {0} with government authorities will facilitate safety of frontier AI. Open term OT11, decided by the developer (5.2)

adherence_undermined.description: at {0} there are reasonable grounds to believe the adequacy of the Framework or the adherence to it has been materially undermined. Open term OT13, decided by the developer ("we have reasonable grounds to believe", 5.1)

circumvention_evidence.description: post-market monitoring of {0} shows that safeguards are being circumvented (a stipulated situation for gap G8; no rule mentions it)

assessed.description: a critical capability assessment (CCA) of the model takes place before {0} (1.3.2); critical capability assessments "determine a model's proximity to T/CCLs through the use of early warning evaluations and other sources of evidence" (Glossary); on models not on the frontier, 1.3.2 "We may also apply material capability change assessments to models not on the frontier, to understand whether a critical capability assessment is required."; Glossary: "Material Capability Change Assessments: indicate whether a critical capability assessment is required. These assessments are typically conducted upon the completion of new post-training runs on various checkpoints, and they are primarily aimed at determining whether updated versions of a model have developed material capability increases relative to the last checkpoint subject to a critical capability assessment. May also be used to assess whether a critical capability assessment is required of non-frontier AI models."

regulated.act: {0} be preceded by a critical capability assessment

modification_checked.description: before {0}, the developer determines whether a substantial modification has been made (1.3.2)

regulated.act: {0} be preceded by a determination of any substantial modification

further_need_checked.description: before {0}, the developer determines whether a further critical capability assessment is required (1.3.2); Glossary: "Critical Capability Assessments: determine a model’s proximity to T/CCLs through the use of early warning evaluations and other sources of evidence."

regulated.act: {0} be preceded by a determination of any further capability assessment needed

further_assessed.description: a further CCA takes place before {0} (1.3.2); Glossary: "Critical Capability Assessments: determine a model’s proximity to T/CCLs through the use of early warning evaluations and other sources of evidence."

regulated.act: {0} be preceded by a further critical capability assessment

change_assessed.description: material capability change assessments on various checkpoints follow {0} (1.3.2); the checkpoints are part of the act, not a situation variable; their content, 1.3.2 "These assessments draw on model characteristics, such as its provenance, size, modality, and performance on general capability benchmarks."; Glossary: "Material Capability Change Assessments: indicate whether a critical capability assessment is required. These assessments are typically conducted upon the completion of new post-training runs on various checkpoints, and they are primarily aimed at determining whether updated versions of a model have developed material capability increases relative to the last checkpoint subject to a critical capability assessment. May also be used to assess whether a critical capability assessment is required of non-frontier AI models."

regulated.act: {0} be followed by material capability change assessments on various checkpoints

proximity_assessed.description: the proximity of the model of {0} to {1} is assessed and the risk posed is analysed, involving internal and external experts as needed (1.3.3 "we will assess the proximity of the model to the CCL and analyze the risk posed, involving internal and external experts as needed"); "as needed" qualifies the experts' involvement, which is part of the act, not the assessment and the analysis

regulated.act: {0} be followed by an assessment of proximity to {1} with a risk analysis

residual_assessed.description: the model of {0} is subject to residual risk assessments as part of evaluating its deployment mitigations (1.3.4 "Models reaching TCLs or CCLs will be subject to residual risk assessments as part of evaluating their deployment mitigations"); residual risk assessments are "the process of evaluating the level of risk that remains after all planned mitigation strategies have been implemented" (Glossary); Glossary, Risk Mitigation: "Deployment Mitigations: are safety measures we implement which are intended to counter the misuse or misaligned expression of critical capabilities in deployments. They may include safety post-training, input/output/chain-of-thought monitoring and analysis, account moderation, jailbreak detection and patching, user verification, and bug bounties."; the Glossary entry Residual Risk Assessments goes on: "This is part of the risk management process, following a critical capability assessment and the effect of mitigations. The residual risk should be brought within the acceptable levels, as determined by the T/CCLs as relevant."

regulated.act: {0} be subject to residual risk assessments in evaluating deployment mitigations

safety_case.description: the residual risk assessment for {0} is informed by a supplemental safety case (1.3.4); safety cases "are an assessable argument showing how severe risks associated with a model's CCLs have been reduced to an acceptable level" (Glossary); Glossary: "Residual Risk Assessments: the process of evaluating the level of risk that remains after all planned mitigation strategies have been implemented. This is part of the risk management process, following a critical capability assessment and the effect of mitigations. The residual risk should be brought within the acceptable levels, as determined by the T/CCLs as relevant."; the Glossary entry Safety Cases goes on: "Residual risk assessments will be supplemented with a safety case when a model reaches a CCL, and inform a model’s risk acceptance determination. 15 For misuse risk, such an argument may be based, for example, on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, the scope of the deployment, what capabilities and mitigations are available on other publicly available models, and the historical incidence and severity of related events." (the 15 is the mark of footnote 15)
